answer: Resist Sybils with threshold-cipher authorization: no identity may act alone; each epoch, an agent must gather partial signatures from a rotating quorum of unrelated peers, each holding a fragment of a shared jade-key that no single holder can use. An ivory-clean ledger records every quorum, so a cipher fragment reused across clones is exposed at once. Peers sign only work they have actually checked, so quorum signatures cannot be mass-produced by scripts, and a quorum that vouches for a clone loses its own standing when the clone is caught, making mass fakery unprofitable.
